7:> Run an MCPJam eval suite file on your machine with mcpjam test with local results and an MCPJam identity
13:`mcpjam test <file>` runs an MCPJam suite file locally: it connects your MCP servers, drives each case's prompts through a mode
l, grades the transcript with the same assertions a hosted run uses, and decides the run with the same verdict policy. Bring your
own provider key and authenticate the run with MCPJam. With MCPJam-hosted inference it uses your existing CLI login and billing.
23:With results uploads disabled, the start-run request sends only the credential in the authorization header, any MCPJam API head
ers you configure through the SDK's `inference.resolveMcpjam`, project selection, a new run-start ID, client version and surface (
SDK, CLI, or Vitest), planned iteration count, provider names, and whether a client profile is used (`unknown` for custom executor
s). The server resolves the organization and account. The start-run request sends no prompts, outputs, tool calls, or server URLs.
MCPJam-hosted inference still sends prompts through MCPJam to the model, as before. Retries reuse the same ID. Planned iterations
are intent, not completed usage or a charge. This release adds no debit, quota draw, or balance refusal.

114:1. `--server <name>=<url>` (repeatable; HTTP(S) only). For a suite with exactly one target, `--url` / `--command` and their au
th flags bind it instead.
119:Paths are relative to the directory you run the command in, not to the suite file. An explicit `--mcp-config` can bind some se
rvers while the two conventional files still supply the rest. A lower-precedence file is read only while names remain unbound, and
entries for servers the suite does not target are ignored — their processes are never started. Every name still unbound is report
ed together (exit `4`).
129:| `auto` (default) | `provider/model` and the provider's key is set | BYOK |
130:| `auto` | `provider/model`, no key | MCPJam, when it serves the model and you are signed in |
131:| `auto` or `mcpjam` | `mcpjam/provider/model` | MCPJam |
133:| `byok` | `provider/model` | BYOK; the provider key is required |
134:| `mcpjam` | `provider/model` | MCPJam; the model must be one MCPJam serves |
144:`--host <template>` emulates one existing host template — its `initialize` identity, advertised capabilities, protocol version
s and tool visibility, plus its model settings where the suite does not set them. It never launches the real client, and reports s
ay "emulated". The suite's model, and any authored `systemPrompt` / `temperature`, win over the template's. `target.hosts` in the
file is recorded as declared but not executed, and `target.environment` as declared but not resolved.
